annotations.keyFindings: Across four hospitals, 17 percent of 2,310 screened patients were anaemic; 61 percent of them were referred, median 19 days from referral to intravenous iron, and 14 percent of referred patients had surgery postponed.
annotations.limitations: Pathways differed between hospitals; recording varied.

annotations.keyFindings: Screening at listing (median 84 days before surgery) led to treatment before surgery for 78 percent of anaemic patients, against 41 percent when screening was at pre-assessment (median 23 days).
annotations.limitations: Screening points used in different hospitals; observational.

annotations.keyFindings: Across 64 centres, haemoglobin thresholds ranged from 120 to 130 g/L, ferritin thresholds from 30 to 100 micrograms per litre, and only 11 centres had a written pathway.
Patients did not understand postponements, described long journeys for short infusions and valued a named nurse.
annotations.limitations: 22 patients from one hospital, invited by the clinic nurse.

annotations.keyFindings: Across 41 reports, services were led by anaesthetists in 19, haematologists in 9, nurses in 8 and general practitioners in 5; only 14 described a reproducible pathway and 9 reported waiting times.
annotations.limitations: Mixed surgical specialties; reports rather than studies.

annotations.keyFindings: Transfusion was 9.8 percent with preoperative intravenous iron and 15.2 percent without, with surgery a median of 12 days later in treated patients.
annotations.limitations: Not randomised; treated patients younger and healthier.

claims.text: Screening at the surgical listing visit, a median of 84 days before surgery, was followed by treatment before surgery for 78 percent of anaemic patients, against 41 percent when screening was at pre-assessment.
claims.passage: 78 percent of those screened at listing received treatment before surgery, against 41 percent of those screened at pre-assessment
claims.interpretation: Where screening happens is a central pathway feature to chart.

claims.interpretation: Referral triggers and ownership vary widely and must be charted.

synthesis: Six retrieved records, appraised at abstract level; four model leads remain unverified. Pathways differ in where screening happens, which values trigger referral, who leads the clinic and how quickly treatment follows. Earlier screening at the listing visit gave far more patients time for treatment than screening at pre-assessment, while referral thresholds varied widely and few centres had a written pathway. A scoping review of service models found that most reports did not describe their pathway in reproducible detail or report waiting times. Patients describe confusion about postponements and long journeys for short infusions. Effectiveness of iron is outside the review's focus; one observational comparison reports less transfusion with treatment but a later operation. The evidence supports a scoping review charting pathway steps, timing, leadership and access.
gradeRationale: Descriptive and observational service evaluations, one survey with response bias and one prior scoping review across specialties; certainty about how pathway features relate to timely treatment is low. Certainty ratings are secondary in a scoping review, whose aim is to map rather than to estimate effects.
summary: Six retrieved records appraised; four source-derived claims; certainty low; four leads unverified.
